profile.entities: Rajratan Global Wire Ltd (Parent); Rajratan Thailand; Rajratan USA
profile.subseg: Bead wire for tires; Steel cord for conveyor belts; Non-tire industrial wire
profile.themes: Raw material cost pass-through lag; Capacity doubling in Chennai; New vertical (Steel cord) pilot; Geopolitical supply chain resilience

deepdive.sec: Specialty Steel Wire & Tire Reinforcement Materials

bull_bear.body: Debt-funded expansion (prefer borrowing at 7-7.5% over equity dilution); active term loan repayment (INR 50cr paid in FY26); working capital borrowing increasing to support US export cycle and inventory build.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material volatility (wire rod prices); Geopolitical disruptions affecting shipping (Singapore/Colombo congestion); Working capital strain from long export credit cycles (US 60+ days); Competition pricing pressure if demand slows; PLI benefit uncertainty (missed targets, lobbying ongoing).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; transparent on Q4 margin miss due to exogenous factors; confident in volume growth and margin recovery; pragmatic on competition (willing to share freight benefits to protect 42-43% market share).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: US subsidiary consolidation adds ~INR 60cr annual logistics cost to P&L (FOB to delivered); Tax rate suppression due to Thailand BOI exemption beyond 36k tons; Steel cord is a 'pilot' for broader wire rope diversification, not just tire reinforcement; Market share recovered to 42-43% from 35-37% lows despite capacity constraints.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Interest outflow declined despite short-term challenges, indicating effective debt management or reduced leverage.
- The deck does not provide explicit details on dividend policy, buybacks, or other capital allocation priorities beyond capacity expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: India: 19% volume growth, Chennai ramping to 35k tons FY27; Thailand: 17% volume growth, limited to 10-14% FY27 due to capacity constraints (55-56k tons); USA: Consolidated entity, high logistics cost impact, 30% growth expected; Non-tire: 14k tons in FY26.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility and margin compression | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Med | As a major wire rod supplier, increased volume demand from Rajratan's expansion offsets margin pressures; Rajratan's volume growth drives upstream consumption. |
| Competitive pricing pressure in specialty wire | Small unlisted wire drawers | loser | High | Rajratan's scale, 42%+ market share, and ability to absorb freight/working capital costs squeeze smaller players facing similar raw material shortages but lacking pricing power. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The Company is the only bead wire manufacturer in Thailand, providing a unique competitive moat in that market.
- It is a leading and trusted supplier of high-quality bead wire to prestigious global tyre customers, with a focus on enhancing market share in India and Thailand.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Market Dynamics] Robust tyre offtake was driven by a sustained rise in passenger vehicle sales and increased vehicle exports, supporting demand for bead wire.
- [Currency Impact] A weakening rupee helped exports during the quarter, partially offsetting cost pressures.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin pressure from INR 10k/ton wire rod increase (Jan-Mar) not passed on; energy costs elevated; FY27 guidance assumes full pass-through; freight savings from Chennai localized sales partially shared with customers to maintain share.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 17-18% volume growth in FY27 (target ~155k tons); Margin: 13.5-14% consolidated (recovery expected Q1FY27); Order inflow: Strong across India/Thailand/US/Europe; Capex/commissioning: Chennai expansion to 60k tons by Q2FY27; Steel cord trials Q2FY27, full production FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Demand exceeds supply; raw material availability is the bottleneck rather than order intake; export pipeline robust in US (+30% growth expected) and Europe (+50% on low base).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Steel cord for conveyor belts (10k ton capacity, INR 150cr peak revenue, ~20% EBITDA margin); Chennai capacity doubling enabling North India penetration; Geographic expansion in Japan and deeper penetration in US/Europe via existing global tire OEMs.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Rajratan achieved record sales volume (+18% YoY) but Q4 margins compressed due to unpassed raw material hikes; guidance implies margin recovery to 13.5-14% in Q1FY27 as prices normalize, while aggressive capex in Chennai (doubling to 60k tons) and new steel cord vertical (INR 70cr) position for 17-18% volume growth in FY27 despite working capital pressures.

open.item: With all three capacities, targeting revenue of INR1,800 crore in next three to four years at current prices
Passed on the ~INR10,000/ton Jan-Mar steel-price increase in Q1FY27; India realization improved above INR90,000/ton and gross margin to be maintained
Chennai to double from 30,000 to 60,000 tons capacity by Q2FY27 via balancing equipment (~INR25 cr more); plan to sell ~34,000-35,000 tons from Chennai in FY27 (from ~17,000)
Targeting ~17-18% consolidated volume growth in FY27, reaching ~155,000 tons of total sales (FY26 was 133,000 tons)
Guiding sustainable consolidated EBITDA margin of ~13.5-14%; not guiding back to 18-20%; margin to recover to ~13-13.5% in Q1FY27 after Q4 RM-driven dip
Thailand FY27 volume growth ~10-14%, from ~51,000 to 55,000-56,000 tons (capacity-constrained, doing debottlenecking)
FY27 export growth plan: North America ~30%, Europe ~50% (low base), Southeast Asia ~10-15%
Long-term loan to reduce to under INR50 crore in FY27 (repaid ~INR50 cr last year); working capital borrowing to rise with volumes/prices/export lead times; prefer debt over equity dilution
No additional capex beyond Chennai balancing (~INR25 cr) and steel cord (~INR25 cr remaining of INR70 cr) for FY27
Steel cord (conveyor belt) / wire rope pilot: total ~INR70 cr capex, 10,000 tons capacity, ~INR150 cr peak revenue in ~2 years (FY29), ~20% EBITDA; trials Q2FY27, capitalize Q3FY27
PLI (8% on incremental Chennai sales, ~INR40-50 cr over 5 years) at risk after missing year-1 and year-2 targets; requested ladder change, no assurance; excluded from projections
Export infrastructure set up 2 years ago now at final customer approvals; Japan emerging as a new opportunity alongside US and Europe, via existing customers' global factories
Positioning 90% recycled steel 'green' bead wire with low scope 1/2/3 emissions to win MNC customers in Europe/North America at 15-20% price premium
No buyback near-term; cash is committed to Thailand and Chennai expansion for growth
